name: alakazam_ml_v25
model: The v20 LightGBM action ranker and v24 card-ID-agnostic target ranker are unchanged. v25 adds three bounded deterministic invariants derived from v24 ladder failures and Yushin Ito's 1000-replay corpus.
model_scope: Hard rules own legality, wins, damage, KO, prize tiers, Boss use, Grimmsnarl pressure, recovery windows, promotions, Dudunsparce pivots, and every non-target decision. The target model contributes at most +/-800 inside deterministic target value.

source_evidence.interpretation: The deck lists are identical. The largest reproducible policy gaps are line-preserving KO promotions, stopping Froslass before powered Munkidori, and avoiding unrecoverable Fezandipiti ex exposure in the mirror.

v25_rule_changes: Prefer Froslass over a powered Munkidori while both are visible on a Grimmsnarl/Froslass board, without inflating the overall MAIN-phase Boss bonus.
Prefer an incomplete Alakazam line over a Dunsparce shield after a KO when the line has the shorter attack ETA.
Keep a truly naked Abra behind Dunsparce so an opening or resource accident still has a one-prize shield.
Track the one-turn Flip the Script recovery window created by an own Active KO.
In the Alakazam mirror, bench Fezandipiti ex only in that recovery window unless it is the only-body survival or Articuno-breaker exception.
Recognize Powerful Hand's 20x-hand damage counters when measuring public Fezandipiti ex KO risk.
preserved_v24_invariants: v24 same-turn ex and Mega ex KO route comparison
v24 Grimmsnarl two-hit pressure and no-route fallback
v22 backup ETA, continuity, Dunsparce rebuild, and backup pre-attachment
terminal Boss and terminal Active win gates
Mist Energy Hammer memory and effect-prevention handling
normal deck floors and exact-KO hand protection
known_limitations: A new live ladder rating has not been measured; improvement above rating 850 is a target, not a validated outcome.
Opponent rating is not preserved in the downloaded replay metadata, so rating-850-plus games cannot be directly bucketed.
Teacher-forced comparison does not simulate the counterfactual trajectory after a changed action.
A recorded expert action is preference data, not proof of a unique globally optimal action.
Opening-hand variance and hidden information cannot be eliminated by deterministic routing.
No official cg package is present locally, so only a source ZIP can be produced.
